transcript:
Header
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Connor Lee (Redwood SE); Jared Kim, Priya Menon, Liam O'Neill, Sara Kong (ClaritySearch)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + reranking endpoints for improving search relevance. Demo of console, embeddings workflow, similarity search + rerank pattern, and discussion of security/SOC2, VPC, and cost/latency tradeoffs. Agreed to run an evaluation with sample data.

Topics:
- Embeddings generation and vector store patterns
- Similarity search + reranking pipeline (embed -> ANN -> rerank)
- Redwood Console quick demo: routes, metrics, Optimize recommendations
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SAML/SSO, audit logs, data residency
- Pricing & next steps for a short POC

Action items (recorded in notes): see metadata list above

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off. We have Diego and Connor from the SE team on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jared: Good thanks, Jared here, head of search at ClaritySearch. Excited to see how you do embeddings + rerank, we've been evaluating a couple options.
[00:15] Priya: Hi, Priya, engineering. We manage the search infra. Appreciate the time.
[00:18] Diego: Great, quick agenda: we'll show the hosted API flows for embeddings, run a similarity search example, then show our rerank endpoint where you can take top-k hits and re-score with a cross-encoder to improve relevance. We'll also touch on Console and Optimize suggestions.
[00:30] Liam: Quick note, our query traffic peaks at about 300 qps and tail latency matters. We want sub-200ms for user-facing queries.
[00:37] Connor: good to know — we'll call that out when we talk about latency/cost tradeoffs.
[00:42] Maya: Before demo, can you quickly share current stack? Vector DB? Indexing cadence?
[00:47] Jared: We're on Elastic for classic search, but vectors are in a mix — some in Pinecone for personalization, some in an in-house Faiss cluster. The indexing job runs hourly, batch updates.
[00:58] Priya: we also use k8s for services, and everything's in AWS VPC. Compliance is important — SOC2, SSO via Okta, keys in AWS KMS.
[01:08] Diego: Perfect, Redwood Hosted API supports embedding creation via REST or SDK. You send docs to /v1/embeddings, we return vectors, you can store in your vector DB, or use our managed reranker pattern if you want.
[01:22] Maya: we'll demo a simple flow: 1) create embeddings, 2) nearest neighbor search with an ANN, 3) call Redwood's rerank endpoint to re-score top-N, returning final ranked results.
[01:30] Connor: We'll also show Console where you can view token-level cost and latency for the calls, plus Optimize suggestions like batching and quantization recommendations.
[01:38] Jared: So question — is rerank running on the same hosted infra or does it call out to a dedicated instance? Latency sensitivity is critical.
[01:44] Diego: Good question. For hosted, rerank is a managed cross-encoder variant running in our hosted fleet. It has options: a low-latency variant for interactive use (higher cost), and a cheaper batch variant for async re-ranking. We can talk SLA and p99 numbers later.
[01:58] Priya: do you support private VPC peering or is data always proxied through Redwood? Security folks will ask.
[02:04] Maya: For Hosted, we have private peering options for enterprise plans and secure TLS in transit; for full isolation you'd look at Redwood Private — but many customers use hosted with VPC peering + KMS integration and SOC2 controls.
[02:18] Jared: ok. Can you show the actual API call?
[02:21] Diego: sure. Demo screen share start...
[02:30] [Screen share: Redwood Console shown]
[02:33] Diego: This is the embeddings endpoint docs: POST /v1/embeddings with model param. Response has vector array. We'll show a small dataset — a set of product help docs.
[02:45] [02:48] Diego: Sending batch of 100 docs, you get back vectors ~768-dim for this model. In Console you can see request latency, token breakdown. Note: transcription: sometimes the docs talk about 7-6-8 dims, but it's 768, sorry — auto-transcript quirk.
[03:02] Connor: For storage you can push vectors to Pinecone, Elastic with vector plugin, or your FAISS cluster. Many customers use Pinecone for managed ANN plus Redwood's rerank.
[03:12] Jared: We already use Pinecone, but the missing piece is cross-encoder rerank that understands query intent.
[03:18] Diego: That's the classic pattern: use a sparse or dot-product approximate search to get top-K, then run cross-encoder rerank to produce final scores. Our rerank endpoint accepts the query and candidate doc texts or ids plus cached vectors and returns scores.
[03:33] [03:35] Diego: We'll do live example — query: 'how do I reset my billing method' against documentation set. First we run a similarity search, top-10 results show some generic hits. Then rerank re-orders by semantic fit.
[03:47] [03:50] Diego: Running similarity: returned in 45ms from our test setup. Top hits show typical partial matches. Now calling /v1/rerank with the query + top-10 document snippets. Rerank returns in ~120ms and improved the precision of top-3.
[04:08] Priya: 120ms per rerank — that's ok for us if it's p95, what's p99?
[04:13] Diego: p99 for this hosted low-latency model is around 300-350ms in our benchmark cluster; p95 around 150-180ms. Those numbers vary with model size and current load. We also offer batching to amortize cost, and we can recommend a smaller cross-encoder model if needed.
[04:28] Jared: cost — how does this map? If we do 300 qps and rerank top-10 for interactive, costs could get heavy.
[04:35] Maya: Right — that's why Optimize suggests batching thresholds and quantization. In the Console under Optimize, you'll see suggestions like 'batch size 8 for embeddings ingest' or 'use 8-bit quantized cross-encoder for rerank at peak hours'. We can model costs in a spreadsheet.
[04:49] Connor: Also, you don't always need full cross-encoder for all queries — implement a hybrid: full rerank for search result pages and a cheaper scorer for autosuggest.
[04:59] Liam: Another question: we use approximate index refreshes hourly — if we do incremental updates, do embeddings replace vectors, and how to handle vector ids?
[05:08] Diego: Typically you upsert by doc id; vectors are versioned and the rerank accepts either raw text or pointer to the doc id plus cached KV cache for short-lived tokens. There's some ambiguity in transcribe — KV cache here refers to model's key-value cache for generation, not your key-value store.
[05:26] Priya: Good clarification. On security: do you allow customer-managed KMS?
[05:31] Maya: Yes — for enterprise we offer KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys for data-at-rest encryption on Private. For Hosted we support customer KMS integration via AWS KMS in select plans. We also provide audit logs and SAML SSO.
[05:43] Jared: Does Redwood store raw texts or vectors on hosted? We need clarity for compliance.
[05:48] Diego: We have retention policies; by default hosted keeps vectors for caching to speed up rerank, but you can opt-out or set retention windows. We'll share the security whitepaper with exact policies.
[05:59] [06:00] Diego: back to demo — here's Console view of a rerank call, trace shows token cost and latency per stage. You can set routes to use cheaper model variants if the primary fails.
[06:12] Maya: also note Redwood's model catalog lists verified performance profiles per model — so you can pick a smaller cross-encoder profile that we validated for rerank latency.
[06:22] Priya: Any pitfalls with embeddings dimension compatibility? Some of our legacy models use 512 dims.
[06:27] Connor: you can choose a model that outputs 512 or 768 dims; the rerank can accept different vector sizes if both sides are consistent, but mixing sizes in the same index requires reindexing or padding strategies.
[06:39] Jared: Great. Can you talk about end-to-end p99 for a query that includes similarity + rerank?
[06:44] Diego: Typical hosted pattern: similarity via ANN (your vector DB) is first — that's usually sub-50ms if Pinecone/FAISS is colocated; rerank is second at ~120-300ms, so end-to-end p95 often under 300ms for tuned setups. For sub-200ms SLAs we might recommend moving rerank to dedicated capacity or using a smaller cross-encoder variant.
[07:02] Priya: So Dedicated vs Hosted — what's the cost delta and operational tradeoff?
[07:06] Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and isolates noisy neighbors. It's higher fixed cost but lower per-token at scale. Hosted is elastic, lower start-up cost, and we manage infra. For strict latency SLAs or data residency you might go Dedicated or Private.
[07:20] Jared: Ok. Let's talk about evaluations — can Redwood run a benchmark with our sample queries?
[07:25] Diego: Yes — we typically ask for a sanitized subset and query logs, then run a bench: embeddings index + top-K retrieval + rerank, and measure latency and relevance metrics (MRR, P@1). We'll share a results sheet.
[07:36] [07:40] Priya: what's the typical sample size?
[07:42] Diego: 10k-100k docs with a few hundred to a few thousand queries is common for an initial POC. For production estimations we scale to your full corpus.
[07:52] Jared: One of our concerns is cold-start cost when reindexing nightly; do you support delta updates efficiently?
[07:57] Connor: yes, incremental upserts are supported; embeddings only need recompute for changed content. Optimize can recommend reindex cadence based on doc churn.
[08:08] [08:10] Maya: i'm going to show the Optimize tab — it flags high-cost routes and suggests quantization or batching. It also surfaces real user traffic patterns so you can set canary rollouts.
[08:20] [08:22] Maya: here's a sample Optimize recommendation: 'for cross-encoder rerank, switch to q4_kg quantized model during off-peak to cut cost 40%'. Note: transcription sometimes munges model tags like q4_k_g into q4kg.
[08:36] Priya: On observability, do you provide per-route tracing and token-level billing?
[08:41] Connor: yes, Console has per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown; you can export to your billing system or S3.
[08:49] Jared: Any rate limits? We'll need predictable throughput at peak.
[08:54] Diego: Hosted has tiers with rate limits; for predictable throughput you can move to Dedicated or request burst capacity. We can set quotas and autoscale policies.
[09:04] Priya: For SSO, you mentioned Okta — do you support SCIM provisioning?
[09:08] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and RBAC are supported.
[09:12] Jared: Great. A couple of other questions: 1) Does rerank accept embeddings as inputs to avoid text transfer? 2) Does Redwood support partial rerank (i.e., rerank only top-5)?
[09:22] Diego: 1) you can pass embeddings directly to rerank to avoid sending raw text, though cross-encoders typically operate on text pairs; we have hybrid endpoints that accept cached embeddings and small snippets. 2) yes you can rerank any top-K subset.
[09:37] Connor: also note that passing embeddings reduces token cost but may change the model's ability to reason on raw text. It's a tradeoff.
[09:44] Jared: That helps.
[09:47] [09:50] Diego: we'll show the API example for rerank now — example payload and response.
[09:56] [10:00] Diego: POST /v1/rerank with body: {query: '...', candidates: [{id: 'doc1', text: '...'}, ...]} returns scores array and reordered ids. In Console you can replay traces and see which candidate got the lift.
[10:12] Priya: Any limits on candidate size?
[10:15] Diego: we recommend snippets under 1k chars; longer docs are truncated or use retrieval-augmented patterns.
[10:22] Jared: How do you handle multilingual docs?
[10:25] Connor: there are multilingual embedding models and rerankers; you can pick per-route model mapping. We'll show language detection suggestions in Optimize.
[10:35] [10:40] Maya: okay let's move through a couple of perturbation examples — show edge cases where similarity picks irrelevant but topically similar docs and rerank fixes it.
[10:50] [10:55] Diego: here's case A: query about 'billing method' — similarity surfaced 'billing overview' and 'billing admin notes' — rerank prioritized the 'reset billing method' doc.
[11:06] Priya: nice, that improved P@1 in this sample.
[11:09] Jared: logs — do we get info on which queries triggered rerank and the before/after scores?
[11:14] Diego: yes, audit logs and traces capture pre/post scores, model id, latency. You can export to your SIEM.
[11:25] Priya: For the POC, we need a security packet.
[11:29] Maya: we'll send SOC2 report, network architecture diagram, and a security FAQ. I'll attach links in the follow-up email.
[11:36] Jared: ok, what's the typical timeline for a POC?
[11:39] Diego: usually 2-4 weeks: dataset ingest + index, run bench, tune rerank threshold. If you want Dedicated/Private, provisioning takes longer.
[11:49] Priya: Team asks about data residency — we need EU region hosting for some customers.
[11:54] Maya: we have EU regions for Hosted and can pin serving to region. For strict residency Private is recommended.
[12:03] [12:10] Connor: i'm going to put a link in chat to a sample benchmark template and deck (link: https://redwood.ai/samples/embeddings-rerank-deck) and a results spreadsheet placeholder (link: https://redwood.ai/samples/benchmarks).
[12:20] Jared: perfect, please include estimated cost model for 300 qps scenario.
[12:24] Maya: will do.
[12:27] [12:30] Priya: one last technical: do you provide client SDKs for vector batching?
[12:34] Diego: yes — Node/Python/Go SDKs with batching helpers and automatic retry logic. They also support streaming embeddings ingestion.
[12:44] Jared: ok, let's recap next steps.
[12:48] Maya: Recap: 1) Redwood to send pricing + trial API key + security docs (Maya) 2) Diego to run a preliminary rerank benchmark using sample subset and share results 3) ClaritySearch to share sanitized dataset and query distribution (Priya) 4) Schedule a follow-up in ~1 week to review bench results.
[13:05] Priya: sounds good.
[13:08] Liam: thanks everyone.
[13:10] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up by Friday.
[13:13] Jared: thanks.
